books.title: Mathematics
books.edition: Reprint 2026-27 (first edition February 2006; revised edition November 2022; reprinted March 2024, June 2024, January 2025 and February 2026)

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's numbered section and subsection headings (Introduction sections are not topics; a parent heading that is only a short lead-in to its subsections is not a separate topic; very short adjacent subsections are joined under one title naming them; section 3.4, which has no sub-headings, is split into two topics at its double-angle identities; where several subsections share a heading such as 'Latus rectum', the topic title adds the curve)

topics.title: Sets and their Representations
objectives: Student can decide whether a collection is a well-defined set and use the symbols for "belongs to" and "does not belong to"
Student can write a set in roster form and in set-builder form and convert between them
visualIdeas: the same set written in roster form and set-builder form side by side

topics.title: The Empty Set
objectives: Student can define the empty (null or void) set and denote it by phi or { }
Student can decide whether a set described by a property is empty
visualIdeas: an empty box labelled { }

topics.title: Finite and Infinite Sets
objectives: Student can distinguish finite sets from infinite sets with examples
Student can state the number of elements of a finite set
visualIdeas: a list that ends beside one that continues with three dots

topics.title: Equal Sets
objectives: Student can define equal sets as sets having exactly the same elements
Student can explain that repeating or reordering elements does not change a set
visualIdeas: two sets with the same elements in a different order shown equal

topics.title: Subsets
objectives: Student can define a subset and a proper subset and use the symbol for "is a subset of"
Student can identify subsets of the set of real numbers such as N, Z, Q and the irrationals
visualIdeas: nested circles for N inside Z inside Q inside R

topics.title: Intervals as Subsets of R
objectives: Student can write open, closed and half-open intervals using bracket notation
Student can represent an interval on the number line and convert it to set-builder form
visualIdeas: a number line with open and closed circles at the ends of intervals

topics.title: Universal Set
objectives: Student can define a universal set as the basic set in a given context
Student can choose a suitable universal set for given sets
visualIdeas: a rectangle containing several sets as the universal set

topics.title: Venn Diagrams
objectives: Student can represent sets and the universal set by Venn diagrams
Student can show relationships between sets, such as a subset, in a Venn diagram
visualIdeas: a rectangle U with circles A and B and their elements placed in regions

topics.title: Union of Sets
objectives: Student can find the union of two sets and shade it in a Venn diagram
Student can use the properties of union: commutative, associative, identity, idempotent and the law of U
visualIdeas: two overlapping circles with their union shaded

topics.title: Intersection of Sets
objectives: Student can find the intersection of two sets and identify disjoint sets
Student can use the properties of intersection, including the distributive law of intersection over union
visualIdeas: two overlapping circles with the common region shaded
two separate circles as disjoint sets

topics.title: Difference of Sets
objectives: Student can find A - B as the set of elements of A not in B
Student can shade A - B and B - A in Venn diagrams
visualIdeas: a Venn diagram with only the part of A outside B shaded

topics.title: Complement of a Set
objectives: Student can find the complement of a set with respect to a universal set
Student can state and verify De Morgan's laws and the properties of complement
visualIdeas: a Venn diagram with everything outside A shaded

topics.title: Cartesian Products of Sets
objectives: Student can define an ordered pair and the Cartesian product A x B of two sets
Student can find the number of elements in A x B and form products such as R x R and A x A x A
visualIdeas: a grid of ordered pairs formed from two small sets

topics.title: Relations
objectives: Student can define a relation from A to B as a subset of A x B
Student can find the domain, codomain and range of a relation and draw its arrow diagram
Student can count the total number of relations from A to B
visualIdeas: an arrow diagram from set A to set B

topics.title: Functions
objectives: Student can define a function as a relation in which every element of A has exactly one image
Student can find the domain and range of a real function
visualIdeas: an arrow diagram where each element of the domain has exactly one arrow

topics.title: Some Functions and their Graphs
objectives: Student can draw the graphs of the identity, constant, polynomial and rational functions
Student can draw the graphs of the modulus, signum and greatest integer functions and state their domains and ranges
visualIdeas: graphs of |x|, the signum function and the greatest integer function as steps

topics.title: Algebra of Real Functions
objectives: Student can add, subtract, multiply and divide two real functions and find the domain of the result
Student can multiply a real function by a scalar
visualIdeas: two functions f and g and the graph of f + g

topics.title: Angles and Degree Measure
objectives: Student can describe an angle as a rotation of a ray from its initial side to its terminal side, positive anticlockwise
Student can use degrees, minutes and seconds to measure angles
visualIdeas: a ray rotating from the initial side with positive and negative angles marked

topics.title: Radian Measure
objectives: Student can define one radian as the angle subtended at the centre by an arc equal to the radius
Student can use the relation between radian and real numbers on a unit circle and l = r theta
visualIdeas: a unit circle with an arc equal to the radius subtending one radian

topics.title: Relation between Degree and Radian
objectives: Student can use pi radians = 180 degrees to convert between degree and radian measure
Student can solve problems on arc length and angles using radian measure
visualIdeas: a table of common angles in degrees and radians

topics.title: Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Student can define the six trigonometric functions of any real number using the unit circle
Student can find where sin x and cos x are zero (x = n pi and x = (2n + 1) pi/2) and the values of the trigonometric functions at multiples of pi/2
visualIdeas: a unit circle with a point (cos x, sin x) and the angle x

topics.title: Sign of Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Student can find the sign of each trigonometric function in the four quadrants
Student can find the values of the other functions given one function and the quadrant
visualIdeas: four quadrants marked with which functions are positive in each

topics.title: Domain and Range of Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Student can state the domains and ranges of the six trigonometric functions
Student can describe how sin x and cos x change in each quadrant and draw the graphs of the trigonometric functions
visualIdeas: graphs of sin x, cos x and tan x over several periods

topics.title: Trigonometric Functions of Sum and Difference of Two Angles
objectives: Student can derive cos(x + y) using the unit circle and obtain cos(x - y), sin(x + y) and sin(x - y)
Student can use identities such as sin(pi/2 - x) = cos x and sin(pi - x) = sin x
Student can use the formulae for tan(x + y), tan(x - y), cot(x + y) and cot(x - y)
visualIdeas: a unit circle with points for angles x, y and x + y used to prove cos(x + y)

topics.title: Multiple Angle, Sum and Product Formulae
objectives: Student can use the formulae for cos 2x, sin 2x, tan 2x and for sin 3x, cos 3x, tan 3x
Student can convert sums of sines and cosines into products and products into sums
Student can prove trigonometric identities using these formulae
visualIdeas: a chain of identities derived from the sum formulae

topics.title: Complex Numbers
objectives: Student can explain the need for complex numbers from equations such as x^2 + 1 = 0 and define i = sqrt(-1)
Student can write a complex number as a + ib and identify its real and imaginary parts, and state when two complex numbers are equal
visualIdeas: the number line extended to a plane of numbers a + ib

topics.title: Addition and Difference of Two Complex Numbers
objectives: Student can add and subtract complex numbers
Student can use the properties of addition: closure, commutative, associative, additive identity and inverse
visualIdeas: two complex numbers added part by part

topics.title: Multiplication and Division of Two Complex Numbers
objectives: Student can multiply complex numbers and use the properties of multiplication
Student can find the multiplicative inverse and divide one complex number by another
visualIdeas: (a + ib)(c + id) expanded with i^2 replaced by -1

topics.title: Power of i and the Square Roots of a Negative Real Number
objectives: Student can simplify any integral power of i using i^4 = 1
Student can find the square roots of a negative real number and explain why sqrt(a) sqrt(b) = sqrt(ab) fails when both are negative
Student can use identities such as (z1 + z2)^2 for complex numbers
visualIdeas: the cycle i, -1, -i, 1 repeating

topics.title: The Modulus and the Conjugate of a Complex Number
objectives: Student can find the modulus |z| and the conjugate of a complex number
Student can use z times its conjugate equals |z|^2 to find the inverse of z and to simplify quotients
visualIdeas: z and its conjugate as mirror images in the real axis

topics.title: Argand Plane and Polar Representation
objectives: Student can plot complex numbers in the Argand plane with real and imaginary axes
Student can write a complex number in polar form r(cos theta + i sin theta) and find its modulus and argument
visualIdeas: a point z in the Argand plane with its modulus r and argument theta

topics.title: Inequalities
objectives: Student can form inequalities from real-life situations described in words
Student can distinguish strict and slack inequalities and linear inequalities in one and two variables
visualIdeas: a word problem turned into an inequality such as 30x < 200

topics.title: Algebraic Solutions of Linear Inequalities in One Variable and their Graphical Representation
objectives: Student can state the rules for adding, subtracting, multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality, including reversing the sign for negative numbers
Student can solve linear inequalities in one variable for x in N, Z or R
Student can represent the solution set on the number line
visualIdeas: a number line with the solution x < 5 shaded and an open circle at 5

topics.title: Fundamental Principle of Counting
objectives: Student can state the fundamental principle of counting (multiplication principle)
Student can count the number of ways of doing successive tasks, such as choosing a pant and a shirt from those available
visualIdeas: a tree diagram of choices of pants and shirts

topics.title: Permutations when all the Objects are Distinct
objectives: Student can define a permutation as an arrangement in a definite order
Student can count arrangements of n distinct objects taken r at a time with and without repetition
visualIdeas: three letters arranged in all possible orders

topics.title: Factorial Notation
objectives: Student can define n! and 0! = 1
Student can simplify expressions with factorials
visualIdeas: n! written as a product of the first n natural numbers

topics.title: Derivation of the Formula for nPr
objectives: Student can derive nPr = n!/(n - r)!
Student can use the formula and n^r for arrangements with repetition allowed
visualIdeas: r boxes filled in turn with n, n - 1, n - 2 ... choices

topics.title: Permutations when all the Objects are not Distinct Objects
objectives: Student can find the number of arrangements of n objects of which p are alike, n!/p!
Student can solve word-arrangement problems with repeated letters, such as ALLAHABAD
visualIdeas: the letters of a word with repeated letters highlighted

topics.title: Combinations
objectives: Student can define a combination as a selection where order does not matter and derive nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!)
Student can use nCr = nC(n-r) and nCr + nC(r-1) = (n+1)Cr
Student can solve selection problems such as choosing a committee or team
visualIdeas: selecting 2 of 4 objects with pairs listed and arrangements grouped together

topics.title: Binomial Theorem for Positive Integral Indices
objectives: Student can observe the pattern of terms, powers and coefficients in expansions of (a + b)^n for small n
Student can build Pascal's triangle and use it to write coefficients
visualIdeas: Pascal's triangle with each number as the sum of the two above

topics.title: Binomial Theorem for any Positive Integer n
objectives: Student can state the binomial theorem using nCr coefficients
Student can expand expressions such as (x + 2)^6 and use the theorem to compute numbers like (98)^5
visualIdeas: the expansion of (a + b)^n written with nC0, nC1, ... nCn

topics.title: Some Special Cases
objectives: Student can write the expansions of (x - y)^n and (1 + x)^n
Student can show that the sum of the binomial coefficients is 2^n
visualIdeas: alternating signs in the expansion of (x - y)^n

topics.title: Sequences
objectives: Student can define a sequence, its terms and its nth term, and distinguish finite and infinite sequences
Student can write terms of a sequence from a formula or a recurrence such as the Fibonacci sequence
visualIdeas: the first terms of the Fibonacci sequence growing

topics.title: Series
objectives: Student can define a series as the sum of the terms of a sequence
Student can write a series in sigma notation
visualIdeas: a series written in sigma notation and expanded

topics.title: Geometric Progression (G.P.)
objectives: Student can identify a geometric progression by a constant ratio between successive terms
Student can find the common ratio of a G.P.
visualIdeas: a sequence 2, 6, 18, 54 with x3 arrows between terms

topics.title: General Term of a G.P.
objectives: Student can use the nth term a r^(n-1) of a G.P.
Student can find a particular term or the number of terms of a G.P.
visualIdeas: a table of n and a r^(n-1)

topics.title: Sum to n Terms of a G.P.
objectives: Student can derive the sum to n terms of a G.P., Sn = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1)
Student can apply the formula to problems such as growth and population
visualIdeas: the sum written above r times the sum and the two subtracted

topics.title: Geometric Mean (G.M.)
objectives: Student can find the geometric mean of two positive numbers as sqrt(ab)
Student can insert geometric means between two given numbers
visualIdeas: two numbers with geometric means inserted between them

topics.title: Relationship Between A.M. and G.M.
objectives: Student can prove that the arithmetic mean of two positive numbers is at least their geometric mean
Student can find two numbers given their A.M. and G.M.
visualIdeas: A.M. and G.M. of two numbers on a number line with A.M. to the right

topics.title: Slope of a Line
objectives: Student can define the inclination of a line and its slope m = tan(theta)
Student can state that a vertical line has undefined slope and a horizontal line has slope zero
visualIdeas: a line making angle theta with the positive x-axis

topics.title: Slope of a Line when Coordinates of any Two Points on the Line are Given
objectives: Student can find the slope of a line through two points, m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1)
Student can use the slope to check whether three points are collinear
visualIdeas: a rise-over-run triangle between two points on a line

topics.title: Conditions for Parallelism and Perpendicularity of Lines in terms of their Slopes
objectives: Student can state that non-vertical parallel lines have equal slopes
Student can state that non-vertical perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is -1
visualIdeas: two parallel lines and two perpendicular lines with their slopes

topics.title: Angle between Two Lines
objectives: Student can find the acute angle between two lines using tan(theta) = |(m2 - m1)/(1 + m1 m2)|
Student can find a slope given another slope and the angle between the lines

topics.title: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
objectives: Student can write the equations y = a and x = b of horizontal and vertical lines
Student can find the equation of a line parallel to an axis through a given point
visualIdeas: horizontal and vertical lines on axes with their equations

topics.title: Point-slope Form
objectives: Student can derive y - y0 = m(x - x0) for a line through a given point with a given slope
Student can find the equation of a line from a point and its slope
visualIdeas: a line through a fixed point with its slope triangle

topics.title: Two-point Form
objectives: Student can derive the equation of a line through two given points
Student can find the equation of a line through two points
visualIdeas: a line through two marked points

topics.title: Slope-intercept Form
objectives: Student can write the equation of a line as y = mx + c using the y-intercept, or y = m(x - d) using the x-intercept
Student can read the slope and intercepts from an equation
visualIdeas: a line crossing the y-axis at c with slope m

topics.title: Intercept Form
objectives: Student can derive x/a + y/b = 1 for a line with intercepts a and b
Student can find a line from its intercepts on the axes
visualIdeas: a line cutting the axes at (a, 0) and (0, b)

topics.title: Distance of a Point From a Line
objectives: Student can derive the perpendicular distance of a point from the line Ax + By + C = 0 using the area of a triangle
Student can find the distance of a point from a given line
visualIdeas: a point with a perpendicular dropped to a line

topics.title: Distance between Two Parallel Lines
objectives: Student can find the distance between two parallel lines y = mx + c1 and y = mx + c2
Student can find the distance between parallel lines given in general form
visualIdeas: two parallel lines with a perpendicular segment between them

topics.title: Sections of a Cone
objectives: Student can describe a double-napped cone and how a plane cutting it at different angles gives a circle, ellipse, parabola or hyperbola
Student can describe the degenerate conic sections: a point, a line and a pair of intersecting lines
visualIdeas: a double-napped cone cut by planes at different angles

topics.title: Circle
objectives: Student can define a circle as the set of points at a fixed distance from a fixed point
Student can write the equation of a circle with given centre and radius and find the centre and radius from its equation
visualIdeas: a circle with centre (h, k) and radius r on coordinate axes

topics.title: Standard Equations of Parabola
objectives: Student can define a parabola using its focus and directrix
Student can write the four standard equations of a parabola and find the focus, axis and directrix
visualIdeas: a parabola with its focus, directrix and a point equidistant from both

topics.title: Latus Rectum of a Parabola
objectives: Student can define the latus rectum of a parabola
Student can show that the length of the latus rectum of y^2 = 4ax is 4a
visualIdeas: a parabola with its latus rectum drawn through the focus

topics.title: Ellipse
objectives: Student can define an ellipse as the set of points whose distances from two fixed foci add to a constant
Student can identify the centre, major axis, minor axis and vertices of an ellipse
visualIdeas: an ellipse drawn with a string fixed at two pins

topics.title: Relationship between Semi-major Axis, Semi-minor Axis and Distance of the Focus, and Eccentricity of an Ellipse
objectives: Student can derive a^2 = b^2 + c^2 for an ellipse
Student can define the eccentricity e = c/a of an ellipse and explain why it is less than 1
visualIdeas: an ellipse with a, b and c marked

topics.title: Standard Equations of an Ellipse
objectives: Student can derive the standard equation x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 of an ellipse
Student can find the foci, vertices, axes and eccentricity from a standard equation, and the equation from given data
visualIdeas: horizontal and vertical ellipses with their foci

topics.title: Latus Rectum of an Ellipse
objectives: Student can define the latus rectum of an ellipse
Student can use the length of the latus rectum 2b^2/a
visualIdeas: an ellipse with a latus rectum through each focus

topics.title: Hyperbola
objectives: Student can define a hyperbola as the set of points whose distances from two fixed foci have a constant difference
Student can identify the transverse axis, conjugate axis, centre and vertices of a hyperbola
visualIdeas: a hyperbola with its two branches and foci

topics.title: Eccentricity of a Hyperbola
objectives: Student can define the eccentricity e = c/a of a hyperbola and explain why it is greater than 1
Student can relate a, b and c for a hyperbola, c^2 = a^2 + b^2
visualIdeas: a hyperbola with a, b and c marked

topics.title: Standard Equation of Hyperbola
objectives: Student can derive the standard equation x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1 of a hyperbola
Student can find the foci, vertices and eccentricity from a standard equation, and the equation from given data
visualIdeas: hyperbolas opening left-right and up-down

topics.title: Latus Rectum of a Hyperbola
objectives: Student can define the latus rectum of a hyperbola
Student can use the length of the latus rectum 2b^2/a
visualIdeas: a hyperbola with a latus rectum through a focus

topics.title: Coordinate Axes and Coordinate Planes in Three Dimensional Space
objectives: Student can describe the three mutually perpendicular coordinate axes and the XY, YZ and ZX planes
Student can name the eight octants formed by the coordinate planes
visualIdeas: three perpendicular axes meeting at the origin with the coordinate planes shaded

topics.title: Coordinates of a Point in Space
objectives: Student can find the coordinates (x, y, z) of a point in space as distances from the coordinate planes
Student can find the octant of a point from the signs of its coordinates and points on the axes and planes
visualIdeas: a point in space with perpendiculars dropped to the three planes

topics.title: Distance between Two Points
objectives: Student can derive the distance formula between two points in space
Student can use it to check whether points are collinear or form a given type of triangle
visualIdeas: a cuboid with two opposite corners as the two points

topics.title: Intuitive Idea of Derivatives
objectives: Student can find the average velocity of a falling body over shrinking time intervals
Student can interpret the derivative as the instantaneous rate of change, such as velocity at an instant
visualIdeas: a table of average velocities approaching a limiting value

topics.title: Limits
objectives: Student can describe the limit of a function as x approaches a value using tables and graphs
Student can find left and right hand limits and decide whether the limit exists
visualIdeas: a graph approaching a point from the left and from the right

topics.title: Algebra of Limits
objectives: Student can state the limit laws for sum, difference, product and quotient of functions
Student can use the limit laws to evaluate limits
visualIdeas: two function limits combining by the limit laws

topics.title: Limits of Polynomials and Rational Functions
objectives: Student can evaluate limits of polynomials and rational functions by substitution and by factorising
Student can use lim (x^n - a^n)/(x - a) = n a^(n-1)
visualIdeas: a rational function with a hole at x = a and its limit

topics.title: Limits of Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Student can state the Sandwich theorem
Student can prove lim sin x / x = 1 and lim (1 - cos x)/x = 0 as x tends to 0 and use them
visualIdeas: a unit circle comparing areas of triangles and a sector for small x

topics.title: Derivatives
objectives: Student can define the derivative of a function at a point and find it from first principles
Student can find the derivative function f'(x) of simple functions from first principles
visualIdeas: a secant line turning into the tangent as h approaches 0

topics.title: Algebra of Derivative of Functions
objectives: Student can use the rules for the derivative of a sum, difference, product (Leibnitz rule) and quotient
Student can apply these rules to combinations of functions
visualIdeas: the product rule written as a two-term pattern

topics.title: Derivative of Polynomials and Trigonometric Functions
objectives: Student can find the derivative of x^n and of polynomial functions
Student can find the derivatives of sin x, cos x and tan x
visualIdeas: graphs of sin x and its derivative cos x one above the other

topics.title: Measures of Dispersion
objectives: Student can explain why a measure of central tendency alone does not describe data and why dispersion is needed
Student can name the measures of dispersion: range, quartile deviation, mean deviation and standard deviation
visualIdeas: two dot plots with the same mean but different spread

topics.title: Range
objectives: Student can find the range as the difference between the maximum and minimum values
Student can explain the limitation of range as a measure of dispersion
visualIdeas: a dot plot with the smallest and largest values marked

topics.title: Mean Deviation
objectives: Student can define the mean deviation about a central value a as the mean of |x - a|
Student can explain why absolute deviations are used
visualIdeas: deviations of data points from the mean shown as distances

topics.title: Mean Deviation for Ungrouped Data
objectives: Student can calculate the mean deviation about the mean of ungrouped data
Student can calculate the mean deviation about the median of ungrouped data
visualIdeas: a table with columns x, x - mean and |x - mean|

topics.title: Mean Deviation for Grouped Data
objectives: Student can calculate the mean deviation about the mean for discrete and continuous frequency distributions
Student can calculate the mean deviation about the median for grouped data
visualIdeas: a frequency table with class marks and |x - mean| columns

topics.title: Limitations of Mean Deviation
objectives: Student can state why mean deviation about the median is unreliable for highly variable data
Student can explain why ignoring signs of deviations makes mean deviation unsuitable for further algebra
visualIdeas: two data sets with similar mean deviation but different spread

topics.title: Variance and Standard Deviation
objectives: Student can explain why squared deviations are used and define variance as the mean of squared deviations from the mean
Student can calculate the variance of ungrouped data
visualIdeas: squares drawn on each deviation from the mean

topics.title: Standard Deviation
objectives: Student can define standard deviation as the positive square root of variance
Student can calculate the standard deviation of ungrouped data
visualIdeas: a bell of data points with one standard deviation marked on each side of the mean

topics.title: Standard Deviation of a Discrete Frequency Distribution

Student can use the formula with sums of f x and f x^2

topics.title: Standard Deviation of a Continuous Frequency Distribution
objectives: Student can calculate the standard deviation of a continuous frequency distribution using class marks
Student can use the alternative formula in terms of the sums of f x and f x^2
visualIdeas: a histogram with class marks at the centres of bars

topics.title: Shortcut Method to Find Variance and Standard Deviation
objectives: Student can use the step-deviation method y = (x - A)/h to simplify calculations
Student can relate the variance of x to the variance of y by multiplying by h^2
visualIdeas: a table with an assumed mean A and step deviations

Student can list the outcomes that make up a given event

objectives: Student can decide when an event has occurred from the outcome of an experiment
Student can identify impossible and sure events, simple and compound events

topics.title: Exhaustive Events
objectives: Student can define exhaustive events whose union is the sample space
Student can identify events that are both mutually exclusive and exhaustive
